title: revenexx Cube Manifest
description: The manifest of a Cube: an extension of the Analytics Studio that brings data and numbers rather than screens or tables. A Cube ships data — a file in its release, rows a function fetches on a schedule, or rows read through a connection the tenant authorises (Google, Meta, Microsoft, LinkedIn, or the tenant's own database or API) — and the metrics, reports and dashboards built on it. Like an app, a Cube never ships SQL and never touches tenant isolation: everything is declared and validated, and the platform loads, scopes and secures the data. The files sit next to cube.json in the Cube root: analytics.json declares the datasets, metrics.json the numbers, reports.json and dashboards.json the surfaces, and billing.json (the same billing.schema.json an app uses) the price and marketplace listing.

$schema.description: Reference to this JSON Schema for editor validation and autocompletion.

name.description: Unique Cube identifier within the vendor (e.g. 'google-ads', 'holidays-de'). Same rules as an app name: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, 2–40 characters. Other packages refer to the Cube's metrics as "<name>.<metric>".

vendor.description: Publisher namespace, shared with apps (e.g. 'revenexx'). A vendor namespace belongs to the first tenant that publishes under it.

version.description: Semantic version (e.g. '1.0.0'), optionally with a pre-release or build identifier.

title.description: Human-readable name shown in the Analytics Studio and the Marketplace.

description.description: Short description of what the Cube adds. Displayed in the Marketplace.

icon.description: The Cube icon: a path relative to the Cube root (e.g. "assets/icon.svg"), an absolute https:// URL, or a Solar icon name in kebab-case (e.g. "chart-2"). Same rules as an app manifest's icon.

tags.description: Free search keywords for the Marketplace.

requires.description: Apps or Cubes this Cube builds on, as name → semver range (e.g. {"orders": "^3.0"}). The Cube cannot be installed without them, because its metrics or reports refer to theirs.

connections.description: External accounts the tenant connects when installing the Cube. The tenant is asked for consent with `reason` and the listed scopes; credentials and tokens are held by the platform and never reach the Cube's files or a report.

settings.description: What the tenant fills in when installing the Cube (an account id, a region, a threshold). Read by the Cube's functions. A 'secret' is stored in the platform secret store and never shown again after it is saved.

data.description: Files in the release that fill a dataset, as dataset → file. Each entry must match a dataset in analytics.json whose source is that file; it is listed here so the release can be checked for it before it is published.

file.description: Path relative to the Cube root, CSV or Parquet.

functions.description: Functions that fetch rows into a dataset, typically from a connection's API. The platform runs them in a sandbox on their schedule, per tenant for a tenant dataset, with the connection's token and the tenant's settings, and writes what they return into the dataset. They return rows; they never get a database handle.

localizableText.description: Operator-facing text. Either a plain string — which the Cockpit shows in every UI language — or a map of BCP-47 language tag to text. 'en' is required and is what the Cockpit falls back to when its UI locale has no entry, so a half-translated file degrades to English rather than to a blank label. Every entry must hold at least one non-blank character.

key.description: Connection key, unique within the Cube. A dataset's `source.connection` refers to it.

provider.description: Who the tenant signs in with. 'google', 'meta', 'microsoft' and 'linkedin' run that provider's consent flow; 'custom' asks the tenant for the connection details of its own database or API (see `kind`).

scopes.description: Provider scopes requested in the consent flow. Ask for read-only scopes; the consent prompt lists every one.

reason.description: Why the Cube needs this connection, shown in the consent prompt (e.g. "Reads your ad spend per campaign and day to compute ROAS.").

kind.description: For a custom connection: a 'database' (queried with `table` or `query`) or a 'rest' API (read with `endpoint`). Required when provider is custom.

key.description: Setting key, unique within the Cube.

type.description: What the field holds. string → a text input; secret → a masked input, stored in the secret store; number → a number input; boolean → a switch; select → a dropdown of `options`.

label.description: Field label in the install form.

required.description: The Cube cannot be installed without a value.

key.description: Function key, unique within the Cube. A dataset's `source.function` refers to it.

dataset.description: The dataset in analytics.json the function's rows are written to.

schedule.description: When the function runs, as a five-field cron expression in UTC (e.g. "0 3 * * *" for daily at 03:00). Omitted, it runs once a day.

timeout.description: Seconds one run may take before it is stopped, at most 300.

max_rows.description: Most rows one run may write, at most 1,000,000. A run that returns more fails rather than writing a truncated dataset.
